source: CK-12 Probability and Statistics Concepts, Section 6.1, CC-BY-NC
notes: Lesson introduces probability via coin/die experiments. Structure: hook (automotive industry) → sample space concept → theoretical vs experimental probability → formula → worked examples × 2 → practice exercises. Mixed text + image units.

units.label: Hook: probability in the automotive industry (text)
units.content_summary: Introduction showing that almost all companies use probability. Automotive companies use it to predict vehicle sales likelihood. Establishes real-world relevance of probability.

units.label: Learning Objectives (text)
units.content_summary: Students will: understand sample space, compute theoretical probability as a ratio, conduct experiments to find experimental probability, compare theoretical and experimental probability.

units.label: Sample space: coin flip experiment (text)
units.content_summary: Definition of experiment (controlled study), sample space (set of all possible outcomes), and event (one possible outcome). Example: flipping a coin → sample space = {heads, tails}.

units.label: Sample space: die roll diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Diagram of a six-sided die with dots labeled 1-6. Shows that sample space for rolling a die = {1,2,3,4,5,6} with 6 equally likely outcomes.

units.label: Theoretical probability formula (text)
units.content_summary: Definition: theoretical probability P(A) = (number of favorable outcomes) / (total number of outcomes in sample space). States that P(A) is always between 0 and 1.

units.label: Worked Example 1: probability of even number from bag (text)
units.content_summary: Problem: numbers 0-9 on paper slips in a bag; one chosen at random. (a) Theoretical probability of even number = 5/10 = 1/2. (b) If repeated 10 times and even chosen 6 times, experimental probability = 6/10 = 3/5. Compare the two.

units.label: Worked Example 2: coin toss experiment (image)
units.content_summary: Tally chart showing results of 20 coin tosses: Heads=12, Tails=8. Used to compute experimental probability and compare with theoretical probability of 0.5.

units.label: Worked Example 2: analysis and comparison (text)
units.content_summary: Calculates experimental P(Heads)=12/20=0.6 vs theoretical 0.5. Explains that as number of trials increases, experimental approaches theoretical (Law of Large Numbers). Key insight articulated.

units.label: Practice: die roll probability questions (text)
units.content_summary: Four practice questions: P(rolling 4), P(rolling even), P(rolling > 4), P(rolling 1 or 6). Students compute each theoretical probability.

units.label: Practice: spinner experiment (image)
units.content_summary: Image of a spinner divided into 4 equal sections colored red, blue, green, yellow. Questions ask for theoretical probabilities and then experimental probabilities after 20 spins (results given).
